newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares up despite slipping in milling.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares up despite slipping in milling.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Wednesday despite some slippage in the dominant milling sector.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index gained 0.5 points to close at 234 points in turnover of an average 23.36 million pounds ($6.9 million).

Recently privatised Arab Cotton Ginning was the most active share, thanks to two transactions worth about five million pounds between them in the last minutes of trading. The close at 35.00 was 0.02 pounds down on Tuesday.
"It looks like some big shareholders are selling them to themselves. You can hardly find any shares in the market, esepcially if you want a big block," said Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB stockbrokers.
Flour mills, one of the mainstays of the Egyptian exchange since partial privatisation earler this year, closed mixed.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills gained 1.09 up at 52.50 but Upper Egypt Flour Mills and East Delta Flour Mills were both down, by 0.20 to 46.00 pounds and 0.40 to 36.00 pounds.
Shares in Medinet Nasr Housing and Development one of the most successful privatisations of the year, hit a record high of 175.00 pounds, 10.00 up on the day.
"There are rumours that the company will give away a free share at the end of this year. It's a very strong company anyway," said Khalil.
When the shares were sold to the public at 65.00 pounds in May, brokers said its real estate assets were worth about six times the valuation implicit in the pricing.
The CMA index for openly traded firms was unchanged at 352.47 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 164.42 from 163.86 on Tuesday.
